# Questions for the client

Answering these will close the open items; the federal figures in `return.json` stand unless the
answers change the facts.

1. **Leo / Form 8332 (2025).** Please confirm you did **not** claim Leo on this return (the agreement
   gives 2025 — an odd year — to his father) and that you signed Form 8332 for him for 2025. If the
   father in fact did not claim Leo and you intended to, tell us before filing — it would change the
   dependent list and possibly Form 8962 household facts.

2. **Elena — remote work facts (affects only New York).** Was your fully-remote arrangement with
   Halvorsen Media Group for your own convenience, or did the company require/structure it for
   business reasons (e.g., the role was restructured, or no New York workspace was available to you)?
   Under the IT-203 convenience-of-the-employer rule, only employer-necessity days keep your Jul–Dec
   wages out of New York source. Same question, briefly, for Marcus's remote work for Reyes & Pike.

3. **Marcus — prior-year basis.** Do you have copies of the filed 2021–2024 Forms 7203 (or the prior
   returns)? We computed beginning 2025 stock basis of **$11,500** from your note and assumed each
   prior year's loss was fully allowed and no shareholder loans exist (you said you never lent the
   company money — please confirm, including advances or credit-card charges you paid personally).

4. **Brooklyn lease.** The file says rent ($1,500) is below market (~$2,600). Please send the current
   lease so we can support that the rent is fair rental for that lease (the library's carve-out from
   the personal-use rule). This is the fact that preserves the $19,550 rental loss allowance.

5. **8962 family size.** Was Leo covered by the marketplace policy (yes per the 1095-A) and a member
   of your household all year (yes per the file)? We used the family-of-4 poverty line ($31,200), the
   only figure in our reference materials. If the correct household count for 2025 is 3, we would
   need the corresponding poverty line — confirm and we will state the effect rather than assume it.

6. **Completeness check.** Any other 2025 items not in the file — Tampa property tax or HOA, other
   brokerage accounts, estimated payments, IRA/HSA activity, other state residency? (None would
   change the standard-deduction conclusion, but estimated payments or refundable-credit facts would
   change line 33/34.)

facts.answer: Elena: the tenant is a stranger, a nurse we found through a broker in 2019. We just never raised the rent.
Marcus: no, I haven't put anything in since 2021 and I never lent it money. Pike guarantees the bank line.
Marcus: the company said remote was fine when I asked to move; they didn't need me out of state. Elena: Halvorsen closed their Tampa office years ago; they approved my request.
Elena: I signed the 8332 for Leo's dad for {TY}, it's his year.
Elena: I got on Halvorsen's plan July 1 when we moved, so we dropped the marketplace plan.
